carries: the swipe never fired because of a SwiftUI rule I kept working around instead of reading: a child's gesture beats a parent's, and the row's Button was the child. simultaneousGesture let the Button fire its tap on release, highPriorityGesture stole the scroll, disabling the row killed the gesture with it — three attempts, three horns of the same problem

the Button is gone: the tap and the drag are siblings on one view, a tap needing no movement and the drag needing twelve points, so SwiftUI tells them apart with no priority claimed over the scroll view
the row keeps its button trait for VoiceOver
recipeByID and resultFor are indexed, cooked is held in memory, and the swipe field is drawn only while a row travels
